BR.name: Caju
BR.citation: NMPPDB; Oxford University Plants 400. Native to northeastern Brazil, used by Indigenous peoples long before European colonization; the Portuguese term derives from the Tupi name acaju, from which the English 'cashew' itself derives (via a mishearing recorded by pirate-naturalist William Dampier, 1699)

IN.name: Kaju
IN.citation: NMPPDB. India is one of the world's largest cashew producers and processors (International Nut and Dried Fruit Council data)

NG.name: Kanju
NG.citation: NMPPDB (Hausa regional name); also documented as Okpokpo (Yoruba) and Akwe olu (Igbo). Nigeria is a major global cashew exporter

US.name: Cashew
US.citation: Gardenia.net; Oxford University Plants 400. Name derives via English pirate-naturalist William Dampier's 1699 mishearing of Portuguese caju

VE.name: Merey
VE.citation: NMPPDB. Native range includes southeastern Venezuela, a center of the species' original diversity alongside northeastern Brazil
